s2.p1: Morocco is only a **provisional** WDSF member. Its member body is the royal federation for aerobics, fitness and **hip hop**, not ballroom.
s2.p2: Partner dancing lives in **salsa** nights in Casablanca, Rabat, Agadir and Marrakech. In breaking, Morocco sent ==Africa’s only breakers== to Paris 2024.

s3.p: joined the **54th National Festival of Popular Arts** in El Badi Palace in 2025: Ahidous, Ahwach, Guedra, Gnaoua, plus a guest troupe from China.

s4.p1: Casablanca-born **Lil Zoo** wins the Red Bull BC One World Final in Zurich, beating Luigi from the US.
s4.p2: It was his ==first BC One win== after five previous attempts. He had already represented Morocco at the 2012 World Final in Rio.

s5.name: AHIDOUS
s5.p: Men and women dance **side by side** in tight rows, to a single bendir drum, handclaps and sung verses called izlan. Its national festival held its 25th edition in 2026.

s5.name: AHWACH
s5.p: Danced in the village square: men in white at the centre, **women in a ring** around them, to tambourine, drum and metal gong. For weddings, harvests and guests.

s6.p: In **Taskiwin**, a High Atlas warrior dance on UNESCO’s urgent list, a saying goes: the dance’s leader, the **raïs**, is more effective than a court judge.

s7.p: Rooted in communities affected by **slavery**, since at least the 16th century, Gnawa blends music with **all-night trance** ceremonies.
s7.p2: Moroccan school **Temps’Danse** wins the country’s ==first-ever gold== at the Dance World Cup, with 36 dancers aged 7 to 24.
